title: fix: Apple chat model controls follow the Gateway catalog

commit.messageHeadline: test(ios): stage focused catalog protocol proof
test(ios): require executed catalog proof with valid fixture
test(ios): initialize proof paths after runner allocation
test(ios): use published selection state in catalog proof
test(ios): prepare native resources and pinned formatting tools
test(ios): isolate pinned tools and retain native formatting proof
fix(apple): consume published session model and sign-in state
test(apple): verify Quick Chat with shared catalog consumers
fix(apple): satisfy native formatting and string inventory checks
fix(apple): negotiate the published catalog capability
fix(apple): disable refused model menu actions
chore(apple): remove completed catalog proof workflow
test(apple): cover catalog recovery and sign-in outcomes

No blocking introduced defect was found, and the latest commit only narrows the sign-in sheet’s visibility. The protected maintainer signal also rules out automatic closure. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `96d910899c49d8db4d60767cf20ab89f555aae66` ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | A coherent owner-based repair with relevant native proof and regression coverage; no blocking correctness finding remains. | | **Proof confidence** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** ✨ media proof bonus | Sufficient (linked_artifact): Retain the supplied native proof assessment: the recorded iOS simulator run exercises the production chat catalog controls and Gateway wizard against an isolated synthetic provider, observing published choices and account status after completion. GitHub confirms the job succeeded; raw artifacts were inaccessible here, and this evidence does not claim external OAuth or device-permission coverage. | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Verified | Sufficient (linked_artifact): Retain the supplied native proof assessment: the recorded iOS simulator run exercises the production chat catalog controls and Gateway wizard against an isolated synthetic provider, observing published choices and account status after completion. GitHub confirms the job succeeded; raw artifacts were inaccessible here, and this evidence does not claim external OAuth or device-permission coverage. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 10 items | Introduced change and review continuity: The pinned merge-base-to-head delta contains the Apple catalog and sign-in changes. GitHub's exact-head commit patch confirms that the only change since the previous reviewed head removes public visibility from the sheet, its initializer, and its body. The prior review contains no findings or published rank-up moves.
Still necessary on main: Inspection of fetched main shows selectedModelSupportsFastMode still returns true unconditionally. The branch instead reads supportsFastMode from the selected published model and preserves the ability to clear an existing override.
Existing catalog negotiation contract: The documented published-model-catalog contract requires capability negotiation and directs older Gateways to update or restart instead of silently substituting local catalog behavior. Both Apple transports implement that contract. | | **Findings** | None | None. | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together The Gateway publishes model choices and owns provider authentication. The Apple apps turn those published facts into chat controls and send selections or sign-in answers back through their captured connection. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Chat session] --> B[Gateway model catalog] B --> C[Apple model controls] C --> D[Session settings request] E[Provider sign-in choice] --> F[Connection-bound wizard] F --> G[Published account status] G --> B ``` ## Before merge - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - An updated Apple app connected to a Gateway without published-model-catalog loses native model choices until the Gateway is updated; slash commands and upgrade guidance remain. This is an intentional, documented compatibility boundary.
Agent review details ### Security None. ### PR surface Other +1096. Total +1096 across 26 files.

### Review metrics | Metric | Value | Why it matters | |---|---|---| | **Production versus test growth** | Production +526 lines; tests +547 lines; localization inventory +23 lines | The production growth principally supplies the shared native sign-in presentation while reusing the existing Gateway wizard and removing client-side capability inference. | ### Merge-risk options **Maintainer options:** 1. **Retain the documented Gateway requirement (recommended)** Accept the explicit older-Gateway limitation with existing slash-command guidance; the current stable Gateway already advertises the required capability. ### Technical review Best possible solution: Keep catalog and authentication decisions in the Gateway, with Apple controls projecting published facts, preserving saved overrides, and explaining unsupported Gateway versions. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Yes, from source: current main advertises Fast support unconditionally and supplies fallback thinking choices independently of the model’s published profile. No local runtime reproduction was executed. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Yes. Consuming the existing session catalog and Gateway wizard removes competing client decisions; the compatibility requirement is already documented and supported by the current stable Gateway. AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. Both Apple transports implement that contract. Public docs: [`docs/gateway/protocol/operator-methods.md`](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/protocol/operator-methods). ([`docs/gateway/protocol/operator-methods.md:175`](https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/protocol/operator-methods), [96d910899c49](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/96d910899c49d8db4d60767cf20ab89f555aae66)) - **Released Gateway supports negotiation:** The v2026.9.4 source defines published-model-catalog and advertises it in the hello response. This establishes released server support, not release inclusion of this Apple patch. ([`src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-hello.ts:160`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3a9d69db306cd7f081e06254cb89c4bcc14a7107/src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-hello.ts#L160), [3a9d69db306c](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3a9d69db306cd7f081e06254cb89c4bcc14a7107)) - **Authentication remains Gateway-owned:** The existing login handler requires administrator scope, revalidates live authority before persistent effects, and binds the wizard to its originating client. Wizard operations check that owner. The new Apple adapters retain the captured socket generation rather than reconnecting requests onto another connection. ([`src/gateway/server-methods/models-auth-login.ts:44`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/96d910899c49d8db4d60767cf20ab89f555aae66/src/gateway/server-methods/models-auth-login.ts#L44), [96d910899c49](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/96d910899c49d8db4d60767cf20ab89f555aae66)) - **Behavioral coverage:** Reviewed tests cover published Fast/thinking projection, unknown versus refused availability, saved overrides, route mismatch, stale catalog responses, older-Gateway slash commands, and sign-in cancellation or completion. The simulator test enters through onboarding and exercises the actual chat controls against an isolated Gateway. ([`apps/ios/UITests/ChatCatalogUITests.swift:6`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/96d910899c49d8db4d60767cf20ab89f555aae66/apps/ios/UITests/ChatCatalogUITests.swift#L6), [96d910899c49](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/96d910899c49d8db4d60767cf20ab89f555aae66)) Likely related people: - **unknown:** The claimed source-line change could not be verified from bounded local history. Runtime, network, CSP, and security claims still need visible diagnostics. ### Workflow - ClawSweeper keeps one durable marker-backed review comment per issue or PR. - Re-runs edit this comment so the latest verdict, findings, and automation markers stay together instead of adding duplicate bot comments. - A fresh review can be triggered by eligible `@clawsweeper re-review` comments, exact-item GitHub events, scheduled/background review runs, or manual workflow dispatch. - PR/issue authors and users with repository write access can comment `@clawsweeper re-review` or `@clawsweeper re-run` on an open PR or issue to request a fresh review only. - Maintainers can also comment `@clawsweeper review` to request a fresh review only. - Fresh-review commands do not start repair, autofix, rebase, CI repair, or automerge. - Maintainer-only repair and merge flows require explicit commands such as `@clawsweeper autofix`, `@clawsweeper automerge`, `@clawsweeper fix ci`, or `@clawsweeper address review`. - Maintainers can comment `@clawsweeper explain` to ask for more context, or `@clawsweeper stop` to stop active automation.

Landed the Apple catalog and sign-in consumers.

- **Bug:** Apple chat could offer Fast or thinking choices that did not match the selected model's published capabilities.
- **Fix:** Shared chat and Quick Chat consume the session catalog. Unknown availability stays selectable; explicitly refused rows are disabled with published guidance. Sign-in shows the code, waits for the wizard result, and then reads published authentication state.
- **Native proof:** [Run 34571594676](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34571594676) passes the iOS simulator flow, 11 projection tests, and 13 Quick Chat tests. Original captures show catalog choices, refusal behavior, the code/link, and connected state after completion.
- **Final CI:** [Run 34577133674](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34577133674) passes on `96d910899c49d8db4d60767cf20ab89f555aae66`. The fresh exact-head local review found no code or security issues and accepted the retained native proof.
- **Additional proof:** 33 Gateway catalog/auth tests, 56 config/state/startup-recovery tests, all 15 real Gateway startup fixtures, and the Telegram Test Server `/models` command sibling passed without inference.
- **Owner-review exception:** [Ayaan's exact-head approval](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/144762#issuecomment-5631382688) waived only the procedural owner-review hold. No CI failure was waived.

The temporary targeted workflow was removed before final review. Simulator proof uses a synthetic sign-in provider and ad-hoc signing; it does not claim external OAuth, release signing, or device permissions. Older Gateways retain slash commands and update guidance.
